title: Observability data lease & sanitization workflow for traces/metrics/logs
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Implement a unified 'data lease' and sanitization orchestration that enforces tenant-aware TTLs, field-level masking, and RBAC-controlled access logging across traces, metrics metadata, and log pipelines. Background: we currently apply ad-hoc retention and redaction in downstream systems which causes gaps in guarantees and auditability. This ticket implements an ingest-side orchestrator (policy engine + pipeline adapters) that enforces per-tenant retention leases, transform-on-ingest masks, and emits immutable access events for any retrievals. Scope:
- Build a policy engine that converts tenant policy (retention days, allowed fields, masking rules, retention exceptions) into executable pipeline configs.
- Integrate the policy engine with trace collectors (OTLP/Jaeger), metrics taggers, and the log ingestion preprocessors.
- Add mask-on-ingest adapters that support deterministic pseudonymization and reversible encryption for fields marked 'reversible' under KMS control.
- Emit access / retrieval audit events to the observability audit stream and wire them into Console dashboards.
Out of scope:
- Long-term archival solution for deleted observations (follow-up ticket).
- Full UI for policy editing (we'll use Confluence-driven policies + infra API for v1).
Technical approach:
- Author a small policy DSL (YAML) for per-tenant leases + masks; store in config-store (vault-backed).
- At ingest, run a lightweight policy evaluator that annotates data with a 'lease_expiry' TTL and a 'mask_profile' applied token. For large payloads use streaming transforms to avoid memory amplification.
- Use KMS-backed reversible encryption for fields marked reversible; fallback to one-way pseudonymization otherwise.
- Emit an audit event for every policy decision and for every read path that causes masked/unmasked access. Ensure events include actor, reason, query_id, and policy_version.
- Provide migration utility to backfill lease_expiry for critical existing streams with a conservative default (30d) and a flag to run per-tenant exceptions.
- Rollout: feature-flag the evaluator; start with low-traffic tenants, verify metrics & dashboards, then widen.
Success criteria:
- All new ingest across traces/logs/metrics includes lease_expiry metadata and a policy_version header.
- No observable perf regression >5% p99 latency on ingest pipeline once feature-flagged in canary.
- Console shows per-tenant retention and masking coverage and access audit events within 30s.
- Security review completed and KMS integration validated.
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL implemented and stored in config-store with versioning
Ingest evaluator emits lease_expiry and policy_version on >95% of events in canary traffic
Mask-on-ingest adapters support both pseudonymization and reversible encryption via KMS
Access audit events contain actor, query_id, policy_version, and are ingested into audit stream
No more than 5% p99 ingest latency regression in canary compared to baseline
comments: 2025-01-16 - Triage: scoped to ingest-side enforcement only. Agreed to keep UI for later and expose control via infra API. Next: design doc.

2025-01-22 - Architecture review with @Javier Ortiz and @Leila Park: recommended streaming transforms and to avoid loading full payloads for masking. Javier suggested a hybrid KMS/pseudonym approach for reversible fields.

2025-02-03 - Prototype: evaluator implemented in python as a sidecar for log-ingest; initial test with 10k events/sec shows ~3% p99 increase. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/412
2025-02-10 - Security review kickoff: requested threat model for reversible encryption, key rotation plan, and audit retention. Assigned to @Nina Patel for security sign-off.

2025-02-18 - QA notes: backfill migration tool found 2 tenants with legacy tags; created migration exceptions list. Monitoring: created dashboard tile for 'policy-evaluator-errors' and 'masked-field-rate'.
2025-02-20 - Canaries expanded to 5 extra tenants. No major incidents. Next: finalize KMS integration tests and add console panels for retention coverage.
